neutral_facts.value: The accused, along with others, were present at a tube well where the deceased was found dead. The accused were armed with weapons and fled the scene after the incident. The deceased was found lying in a pool of blood with a gunshot wound. The prosecution relied on eyewitness accounts and medical evidence to establish the presence of the accused at the scene and their involvement in the incident. The accused were identified by witnesses based on their weapons and proximity to the shed. The investigation included the recovery of cartridges and a postmortem report indicating the cause of death was a gunshot injury. The trial court convicted the accused under Section 302 read with Section 34 IPC, sentencing them to life imprisonment. The High Court upheld the conviction. The accused were examined by the court, and their testimonies were scrutinized. The Supreme Court affirmed the conviction, noting the presence of the accused at the scene and their involvement in the incident, despite the absence of injuries caused by the lathi or ballam. One of the accused was found to be a juvenile and was released from custody.

defence_argument.value: The defence argued that there was no common intention among the accused, as the prosecution's case relied on testimonies that were not reliable. They pointed out that the medical evidence did not show any injuries caused by the lathi or ballam, and that the absence of such injuries undermined the conviction under Section 34 IPC. They also highlighted the non-examination of certain witnesses and the juvenile status of Vijendra Singh.
